title: Di Resta beats Auer to win Hungaroring Race 1 for Mercedes
dek: Paul di Resta turned pole position into victory at the Hungaroring, finishing 0.587 seconds ahead of Mercedes team-mate Lucas Auer after the two swapped the lead through the pit-stop phase.

chapters.title: A one-point title fight leaves Germany
text: The DTM left Germany for the first time in 2018 when it reached the Hungaroring on 1–3 June, and it did so with the championship balanced on a single point. BMW's Timo Glock had defended the lead at the Lausitzring and arrived on 72 points, one clear of Gary Paffett on 71, with Pascal Wehrlein third on 39. Mercedes-AMG, who would leave the series at the end of the year, had won three of the first four races, while Audi had struggled badly at Hockenheim and the Lausitzring and travelled to Hungary without the favourite's tag it had carried the year before. BMW had put a car on the podium in each of the first four races, and its motorsport director, Jens Marquardt, wanted more of the same in Hungary. Reigning champion René Rast was back in the car after missing the Lausitzring Sunday race following his heavy crash there.

The Hungaroring is a twisty, 4.381-kilometre layout in a natural basin, where the heat builds quickly and the tyres suffer from the constant braking and acceleration. With 14 corners and little room to pass, the best chance to overtake comes at the tight right-hander at the end of the 800-metre start-finish straight, which put a premium on grid position and on the timing of the compulsory pit stop.

There was an unusual visitor in the BMW garage: Alex Zanardi spent the weekend shadowing the team to learn how a DTM operation works, ahead of a guest drive in a modified M4 at Misano in August. Each race on the weekend was scheduled for 55 minutes plus one lap, and Saturday's would run to 34 laps.

chapters.title: Di Resta takes pole after Auer runs wide on his last lap
text: Rain fell before Saturday morning's practice and made for a slippery rehearsal, but the track had dried by the time the 18 cars went out for qualifying in bright sunshine. Auer set the early marker with a 1m37.564s that put him six tenths clear of Paffett, until the Audis, who had held back their first runs, came out and Nico Müller beat him by a little under a tenth.

The session then went quiet before a flurry of improvements in the final minute. Paul di Resta cut the benchmark to 1m37.349s, a tenth faster than Müller's best, and Auer was on course to beat the Scot after setting the quickest first sector. He ran wide at Turn 9, however, and could not improve, which left di Resta on pole for Mercedes-AMG Motorsport Remus with Müller's Abt Audi alongside, 0.135 seconds back, and Auer third on 1m37.564s.

René Rast held fourth for Team Rosberg on 1m37.598s, ahead of the Mercedes pair of Edoardo Mortara and Daniel Juncadella, who were separated by two thousandths of a second. Jamie Green slipped to seventh, and Augusto Farfus was the best of the BMWs in eighth, more than half a second off the pace. Paffett could manage only ninth, while Glock, the points leader, qualified 16th after getting the timing of his second run wrong. Audi had three cars in the top seven, a clear step forward after the first two rounds.

chapters.title: BMW and Green gamble on a first-lap stop
text: Di Resta led away cleanly, and Müller kept second place after a brief battle with Auer. The Mercedes driver got his nose ahead at Turn 2, only for the Audi to take the place back a corner later. Behind them Mortara went past Rast for fourth on the opening lap.

The most aggressive strategies came straight away. At the end of the first lap Green, Bruno Spengler and Philipp Eng all dived into the pits for their mandatory stops, and a lap later Glock and Joel Eriksson did the same, so that four of the six BMWs were on fresh tyres almost before the race had begun. A few spots of rain were reported shortly afterwards, but the shower never developed and the hot asphalt dried the drops almost at once.

Up front, di Resta and Müller opened a lead of around a second over the rest. Auer was the first of the leaders to stop, coming in on lap six together with Farfus, and that choice would shape the afternoon.

chapters.title: Auer's earlier stop pays off, then di Resta strikes back
text: Di Resta waited three more laps and did not get the best of stops, and although he came out still in front, Auer, on warmer tyres, passed him easily at Turn 2. Müller changed tyres on the following lap and also rejoined ahead of Auer, but the Mercedes driver found a way past him as well. Di Resta later admitted that the stop was not the team's best and that Müller's must have been quicker.

The Scot then passed Müller after a short fight, and that tussle let Auer pull out a gap of more than two seconds. Auer said he had pushed very hard after his stop to undercut both of them, and that he then had to look after his used tyres when di Resta came back at him.

chapters.title: Late stoppers and early gamblers sort the midfield
text: Elsewhere the order was settled by a mix of strategies. Mortara, who had stayed out longest of the front runners, stopped on lap 14 and Rast a lap after, and the reigning champion took fourth place from the Italian with a forceful move once both were on new tyres. Paffett, who did not stop until lap 16, climbed from ninth on the grid to sixth. Robin Frijns and Loïc Duval, together with Mike Rockenfeller, ran far longer than the rest on their first set of tyres, and the first two had the best pace of anyone in the closing stages, moving up to seventh and eighth from 14th and 11th on the grid.

chapters.title: Auer lets di Resta by and the Mercedes one-two is sealed
text: With the race past its midpoint, di Resta closed in on his team-mate and went by before Turn 2. From there the lead was never in danger for the last 15 minutes or so, and di Resta took the flag 0.587 seconds clear after 34 laps and 57m13.199s. It was his first win of 2018 and Mercedes' fourth in five races this season. Auer, who also set the fastest lap, a 1m38.812s on lap 10, completed the one-two for the Stuttgart brand.

Müller held on for the final podium place, 2.236 seconds behind the winner and his first top-three finish of the year, with Rast 0.662 seconds further back after a close fight in the last laps. Mortara was fifth, 6.695 seconds adrift, and Paffett sixth, 12.166 seconds behind di Resta. That result was enough for Paffett to retake the lead of the championship, on 79 points, seven clear of Glock, with di Resta up to third on 56.

For BMW it was a day to forget. The best of the six M4s was Spengler in 12th, Glock was 14th, and no BMW scored a point after the early-stop tactics failed to pay off. The team said that the balance of the cars had not been right in qualifying or in the race, and promised a big step for Sunday.

facts.v: Paul di Resta won from pole position, 0.587 seconds ahead of Lucas Auer, for Mercedes' fourth win in the first five races of 2018.
